Java expert analyzing a bug report and the corresponding changes made to fix the bug.
Analyze the bug report and the seed changes to provide evidence for refining the initial impact set.

You are an experienced Java developer with an excellent understanding of code changes and their impact on other code entities.

Analyze the Jira bug report title and description and the seed changes that were made to fix the reported bug. Combine this analysis with the initial static impact set, which contains the fully qualified names of code entities that are statically related to the seed changes.
For each entity in the initial static impact set, analyze its relationship to the seed changes and collect evidence indicating whether the entity must be modified as a consequence of the seed changes.  Furthermore, identify any additional code entities that must be modified or created and collect supporting evidence.
Focus on production code, not test code or other files.
Inputs: - Jira bug report title: Resolve does not deliver all dependent artifacts - Jira bug report description: We have three configurations.

{code:title=Configurations}
<configurations>
 <conf name="runtime" extends="requires, compile" transitive="true"/>
 <conf name="requires" />
 <conf name="compile"/>
</configurations>
{code}

Additional we have the following dependencies between ivy modules (test, a, b, c) (each module has a simple jar as artifact):
{code:title=Dependencies}
test "requires->#" a
test "requires->#" c

c "requires->#" a
c "requires->#" b
{code}
The artifacts have the configuration compile.

If I do a resolve on test with configuration "runtime" I only get artifacts for modules a and c but not b. 

The problem happens in conflict resolution. Ivy generates the dependendies with wrong rootModuleConfigurations. In out case, the module b is loaded with root module configuration requires and not runtime.

You find attached the example a unit test and a possible resolution in method computeConflicts of ResolveEngine.

Possible dependency to IVY-729 - Seed changes and their Git diff hunks: [{"fqn": "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])", "git_diff_hunk": "@@ -291 +291 @@ public class IvyNode implements Comparable {
- public Collection getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs) {
+ public Collection getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs, String requestedConf) {
@@ -305 +305 @@ public class IvyNode implements Comparable {
- deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], confs[i]));
+ deps.addAll(getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], requestedConf));"}] - Initial static code change impact set: ["org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()", "org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.isRoot()", "org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)"]

Expected output:
Structured evidence for each entity of the initial static impact set, including: - its fully qualified name - an assessment of whether it must be modified as a consequence of the seed changes - the supporting evidence
Additionally, include any code entities that must be modified or created but are not part of the initial static impact set.

message.content:
# Analysis of Bug and Seed Changes

## Understanding the Bug

The bug is in Ivy's conflict resolution. When resolving configuration `runtime` (which extends `requires, compile` transitively), module `b` is loaded with `rootModuleConfigurations = requires` instead of `runtime`. The root cause is in `IvyNode.getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs)`: when iterating over the requested configurations, it passes `confs[i]` as the `requestedConf` argument to the recursive `getDependencies` call, rather than propagating the original `requestedConf` from the caller. This causes the wrong `rootModuleConfigurations` to be attached to transitively discovered dependencies, so conflict resolution (which uses `rootModuleConfigurations`) drops module `b`.

The seed change fixes this by adding a `requestedConf` parameter to `getDependencies(String, String[])` and propagating it (instead of `confs[i]`) into the recursive call.

## Evidence for Each Entity in the Initial Static Impact Set

### 1. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)`

- **Must be modified: YES (this is the core seed change).**
- **Evidence:** The seed diff shows the signature of `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs)` is changed to `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs, String requestedConf)`, and the recursive call `getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], confs[i])` is changed to `getDependencies(rootModuleConf, confs[i], requestedConf)`. The three-argument overload `getDependencies(String, String, String)` is the target of that recursive call. Its semantics must be consistent with the new contract: the third argument is now the *original* requested configuration (propagated from the root of the resolution), not the intermediate configuration being traversed. Any logic inside this method that uses the third parameter to compute `rootModuleConfigurations` (e.g., when building `IvyNode` dependencies via `getDependencies`/`getAllConfigurations`) must be verified to correctly use the propagated `requestedConf`. This is the method whose behavior the bug report explicitly identifies as producing "wrong rootModuleConfigurations."

### 2. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)`

- **Must be modified: YES (likely, per the bug report's suggested resolution).**
- **Evidence:** The bug report explicitly states: "You find attached the example a unit test and a possible resolution in method computeConflicts of ResolveEngine." Conflict resolution is where the symptom manifests (module `b` is dropped because its `rootModuleConfigurations` is `requires` rather than `runtime`). Even with the `IvyNode.getDependencies` fix propagating `requestedConf`, `computeConflicts` must be checked to ensure it compares/merges `rootModuleConfigurations` correctly (e.g., unioning configurations rather than taking the first-seen one). The bug report names this method as the location of a possible fix, so it is a strong candidate for modification.

### 3. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.isRoot()`

- **Must be modified: NO (no direct evidence).**
- **Evidence:** `isRoot()` is a simple predicate used to distinguish the root node from dependency nodes. The seed change alters how `requestedConf` is propagated during dependency traversal; it does not change what constitutes a root node. There is no indication in the bug report or diff that root detection logic is wrong. This entity appears in the static impact set only because it is called within the dependency-resolution path, not because its behavior needs to change.

### 4. `org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()`

- **Must be modified: NO (no direct evidence).**
- **Evidence:** This method simply returns the names of all configurations declared on a module descriptor. The bug is about which `rootModuleConf`/`requestedConf` is propagated during traversal, not about enumerating configuration names. The seed diff does not touch configuration-name enumeration. It appears in the static impact set because `getDependencies` iterates over configuration names, but the fix is in the propagation of `requestedConf`, not in how names are obtained.

### 5. `org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()`

- **Must be modified: NO (no direct evidence).**
- **Evidence:** Same reasoning as `getConfigurationsNames()`. This method returns public configuration names and is used when computing which configurations to traverse. The bug is not that the wrong set of configuration names is returned; it is that the wrong `requestedConf` is passed down the recursion. No change to this method is warranted by the seed diff or bug description.

## Additional Code Entities That Must Be Modified or Created (Not in Initial Static Impact Set)

### A. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])` — signature change / callers

- **Must be modified: YES.**
- **Evidence:** The seed diff changes the signature of this method from `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs)` to `getDependencies(String rootModuleConf, String[] confs, String requestedConf)`. Every caller of the two-argument form must be updated to pass the appropriate `requestedConf`. This includes callers within `IvyNode` itself (e.g., `getAllConfigurations`, `getDependencies(String conf)` overloads, `getRealConfs`, `getConfigurations`, and any `getDependencies` variants used by `ResolveEngine`/`VisitNode`). The initial static impact set lists the three-argument overload but not the two-argument one whose signature is actually changed — this is a gap that must be addressed.

### B. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String)` (single-conf overload) and other `getDependencies` overloads

- **Must be modified: YES (call-site updates).**
- **Evidence:** These overloads delegate to the array-based `getDependencies`. Since the array-based method's signature changes, all delegating overloads must be updated to supply a `requestedConf` (typically the same `conf` being requested). Without this, compilation fails and/or the propagation contract is broken.

### C. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode` (and its `getDependencies`/`loadDependencies` usage)

- **Must be modified: YES (call-site updates).**
- **Evidence:** `VisitNode` is the traversal structure used by `ResolveEngine` and is a parameter type in `computeConflicts`. It invokes `IvyNode.getDependencies(...)` during traversal. Because the signature of the array-based `getDependencies` changes, `VisitNode`'s calls must be updated to pass the propagated `requestedConf`. This entity is not in the initial static impact set but is a direct caller in the resolution path.

### D. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine` (other methods invoking `getDependencies`)

- **Must be modified: YES (call-site updates).**
- **Evidence:** `ResolveEngine` (including `computeConflicts` and the resolution loop that builds `VisitNode`s) calls `IvyNode.getDependencies`. With the signature change, these call sites must be updated to pass the correct `requestedConf` (the root module configuration being resolved). The bug report's suggested fix in `computeConflicts` is consistent with this.

### E. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode` — `rootModuleConfigurations` handling (fields/accessors)

- **Must be modified: YES (behavioral verification / possible adjustment).**
- **Evidence:** The bug report states the symptom is that "the module b is loaded with root module configuration requires and not runtime." The `rootModuleConfigurations` field (and its accessors such as `getRootModuleConfigurations`/`addRootModuleConfiguration`) is populated during dependency creation. With the corrected `requestedConf` propagation, the code that records `rootModuleConfigurations` must be verified to use the propagated `requestedConf` (the original root configuration) rather than the intermediate `confs[i]`. If the recording logic currently uses the third parameter directly, it will now receive the correct value; if it uses a different source, it may need adjustment. This is the entity whose incorrect state causes the bug, so it must be validated/modified as part of the fix.

### F. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(...)` — `getAllConfigurations` / `getRealConfs` helpers

- **Must be modified: YES (call-site updates).**
- **Evidence:** These helpers compute the set of configurations to traverse and call `getDependencies`. Since the array-based `getDependencies` signature changes, these helpers must be updated to pass `requestedConf` through. They are part of the same class and are on the traversal path that produced the wrong `rootModuleConfigurations`.

## Summary Table

| Entity | Must Modify? | Key Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String,String,String)` | Yes | Target of seed diff; must honor propagated `requestedConf` for `rootModuleConfigurations` |
| `ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(...)` | Yes | Bug report names it as location of possible fix; conflict resolution drops module `b` |
| `IvyNode.isRoot()` | No | Predicate unrelated to `requestedConf` propagation |
| `ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()` | No | Enumeration of names unaffected by propagation fix |
| `ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()` | No | Same as above |
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String,String[])` | Yes (not in set) | Signature changed by seed diff; all callers must update |
| `IvyNode.getDependencies(String)` and other overloads | Yes (not in set) | Delegate to changed array-based method |
| `VisitNode` | Yes (not in set) | Calls `getDependencies` during traversal |
| `ResolveEngine` (other call sites) | Yes (not in set) | Calls `getDependencies`; must pass `requestedConf` |
| `IvyNode` `rootModuleConfigurations` field/accessors | Yes (not in set) | Incorrect value is the root cause; must be populated from propagated `requestedConf` |
| `IvyNode.getAllConfigurations`/`getRealConfs` | Yes (not in set) | Helpers on traversal path calling changed method |
